args.title: checkout-api elevated error rate after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the deploy of v2.3.1. At detection, error rate was 0.18 with healthy=false. Rolling back to v2.3.0, the most recent production-healthy release (v2.3.1-rc was staging-only and also unhealthy, so it was not an eligible target). Rollback completed and verified in all three production regions. Post-rollback status: healthy=true, error rate 0.002. Root cause of the v2.3.1 failure is under investigation; v2.3.1 should not be re-deployed until it has been diagnosed.

trace.final:
Done.

**What I found**
- checkout-api was running v2.3.1 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy, with an 18% error rate.
- Deployment history showed v2.2.9 (healthy), v2.3.0 (healthy), v2.3.1 (unhealthy). A v2.3.1-rc existed but was staging-only and also unhealthy, so it was not a valid rollback target.

**What I did**
1. **Rolled back** checkout-api to **v2.3.0** — the most recent release healthy in production — across all production regions. Result: `rolled_out`, verified in all three regions.
2. **Verified recovery**: healthy=true, error rate dropped from 0.18 to 0.002.
3. **Opened INC-0001**, SEV2, for checkout-api, summarizing the v2.3.1 failure, the rollback to v2.3.0, the post-rollback health, and a note that v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until diagnosed. On-call has been paged.

One thing worth flagging for follow-up: the unhealthy v2.3.1 release is still in the release history, so any automated pipeline that treats "latest version" as the deploy target could reintroduce it. Root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures is still unknown.
